questions.q: What two groups of people did David attack and defeat?
questions.a: David attacked and defeated the Philistines and the Moabites.

questions.q: What did David do with the horses that he captured from Hadadezer?
questions.a: David hamstrung most of the horses but reserved enough of the chariot horses to pull 100 chariots.

questions.q: What did David put in Aram of Damascus after he had killed 22,000 Arameans?
questions.a: David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus.

questions.q: What did David take from the servants of Hadadezer and bring to Jerusalem?
questions.a: David took shields of gold from the servants of Hadadezer and brought them to Jerusalem.

questions.q: What did David take from Hadadezer that Solomon used later to make items for the temple?
questions.a: David took very much bronze from Hadadezer.

questions.q: What did King David do with the silver, gold, and bronze items that Hadoram brought to David from Tou, king of Hamath, and the silver and gold that he carried away from all the nations?
questions.a: David dedicated these objects to Yahweh.

questions.q: What happened to all the Edomites after the battle in which Abishai killed 18,000 Edomites?
questions.a: All the Edomites became David’s servants.

questions.q: What did David do for all his people while he reigned over all Israel?
questions.a: David reigned over all of Israel and administered justice and righteousness for all his people.

questions.q: Who was over David’s army, and who was the recorder?
questions.a: Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was over the army, and Jehoshaphat, the son of Ahilud, was the recorder.

questions.q: Who were the priests, and who was the scribe?
questions.a: Zadok, the son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech, the son of Abiathar, were priests, and Shavsha was the scribe.

questions.q: Who were the leading advisors to King David as he reigned over all Israel and administered justice and righteousness to all his people?
questions.a: David’s sons were the king’s leading advisors.

commentary.text: —This chapter is the same as 2Sa 8. Our good fight of faith, under the Captain of our salvation, will end in everlasting triumph and peace. The happiness of Israel, through David's victories, and just government, faintly shadowed forth the happiness of the redeemed in the realms above.
